chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about kohl that is kneaded with Nabidh (fermented drink), is that permissible? So he said: No.

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh (fermented drink, typically of grapes or dates)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use Nabidh for kneading kohl?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the permissibility of using Nabidh as a binding agent for kohl is negated, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that if a substance is consumed as a drink, it is generally considered impure (najis) or unsuitable for medicinal application unless specifically exempted. This ruling highlights the distinction between Nabidh's status as a beverage versus its utility in external applications, a topic of debate among scholars regarding the threshold of intoxication and purity. The chain of transmission through Ali ibn Ja'far and his brother Musa al-Kazim underscores the reliability of the Ahl al-Bayt's direct legal insights in al-Kafi.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the kohl kneaded with Al-Nabeez, is that correct (to apply in the eyes)?’ So heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from a number of our people from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn Ja‘far who has said the following: “I once asked my brother, abu al-Hassan ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about kohl made into dough with al- Nabidh; if it is proper. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not proper.’”
